texts.li: [entertainers] {FACTION} have set a place at their festival for the colony's entertainers, as their council promised: players, singers, whoever the colony sends, to play for {PLACE} and stay for the day. {HOST} sent the word.
[entertainers,their:lowtech] Word came from {PLACE}: the fires are being built for their festival, and the colony's players and singers are awaited, as the elders agreed.
[entertainers,their:hightech] {PLACE} has the colony's entertainers on the festival's programme, between the parade and the dance. {HOST} signed the note.
[invited] {FACTION} keep their festival at {PLACE}, and {HOST} asks the colony's people to come and sit at their tables for it, as the colony agreed in its letter.
[invited,their:lowtech] A runner from {PLACE} brought word of the festival: the drums are ready, and the colony's people are awaited, as they promised.

li.label: Send the colony's people
li.outcome: Places will be kept for the colony's people at {PLACE}.

li.label: Not this time
li.outcome: {FACTION} are sorry, and keep their festival all the same.

terms.li: At least two of the colony's people at {PLACE} by caravan within {DAYS} of the colony agreeing (it's about {TALE} away), staying for the festival, about half a day at the town. The caravan only needs to reach the town and wait there; whoever goes plays for them.\n\nThey go home with a gift worth about {COUNT} silver, and {FACTION} will remember who came. If no one does, they'll notice that too.

accepted.li: The colony will send its people to {PLACE}. Form a caravan of at least two and send it there within {DAYS}.
[entertainers] The colony's entertainers will go to {PLACE}. Send a caravan of at least two there within {DAYS}.

ready.li: The colony's people have reached {PLACE} for the festival, and room has been made for them. Keep the caravan there until the day is over.
[entertainers] The colony's entertainers are at {PLACE}, and the crowd is gathering. Keep the caravan there until the festival is over.

reminder.li: The festival at {PLACE} is coming, and the colony's people haven't arrived.

done.li: [attended,entertainers] The colony's entertainers played the festival at {PLACE} to the end, and {FACTION} sent them home with gifts: {ITEM}.
[attended,invited] The colony's people kept the festival at {PLACE} with {FACTION}, and came home with gifts: {ITEM}.
[attended] The colony's people were made welcome at {PLACE}'s festival and came home with gifts: {ITEM}.
[brief] The colony's people reached {PLACE} but didn't stay to the end. {FACTION} were glad they came at all.

fail.li: [absent] {FACTION} kept their festival at {PLACE} without the colony, and noticed the empty places.
[absent] Nobody from the colony came to the festival at {PLACE}, after all that was promised.

cancelled.li: The festival at {PLACE} is no longer awaited.
